blindWork: n(Al2(SO4)3) = 0.0250 L x 0.200 M = 5.00e-3 mol, so n(SO4^2-) = 3 x 5.00e-3 = 1.50e-2 mol. BaCl2 supplies one Ba2+ per formula unit, so n(BaCl2) = 1.50e-2 mol. V = 1.50e-2 / 0.150 = 0.1000 L = 100.0 mL.
stem: Precipitation / Stoichiometry: What volume of $0.150\text{~M}\text{~BaCl}_{2}$ is required to completely precipitate all the sulfate ions from $25.0\text{~mL}$ of $0.200\text{~M}\text{~Al}_{2}\left( \text{SO}_{4} \right)_{3}$ solution?
sourceExplanation: Stoichiometric ratio: $3\text{~Ba}^{2 +} \sim 2\text{~Al}_{3}\left( \text{SO}_{4} \right)_{3}$. Moles of $\text{SO}_{4}^{2 -} = 2 \times (0.0250 \times 0.200) = 0.010\text{~mol}$. Required $\text{Ba}^{2 +} = 0.010\text{~mol}$, volume $= 0.010/0.150 = 0.0667\text{~L} = 66.7\text{~mL}$? Wait, check: $n\left( \text{Al}_{2}\left( \text{SO}_{4} \right)_{3} \right) = 0.025 \times 0.200 = 0.005\text{~mol}$. Each mole contains $3$ moles of $\text{SO}_{4}^{2 -}$, so $0.015\text{~moles~of~}\text{SO}_{4}^{2 -}$. $\text{Ba}^{2 +} + \text{SO}_{4}^{2 -} \rightarrow \text{BaSO}_{4}$. So $0.015\text{~moles~of~}\text{BaCl}_{2}$ needed. $V = 0.015/0.150 = 0.100\text{~L} = 100.0\text{~mL}$. (Correct option: D)
